steps.text: The Catastrophe cloud in the sky has not yet dissipated.
Should you take off your gloves, you would be able to feel the Originium dust in the air scratching the palm of your hand.
The Nachzehrer King sits atop his throne, casting his eyes across his army.
The Nachzehrer's army will not be shaken. The Nachzehrer's army will not show weakness.
They pass through the storm, beyond injuries, and over the carcasses of compatriots and enemies alike.
The Sarkaz continue to march. Until the enemies of the Nachzehrer King are completely crushed, they have no right to stop.
'They are War itself.'

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Your Grace, we've sustained heavy losses. Nearly a third of the high-speed battleships in the vanguard's squadron have been incapacitated. We're trying to turn the situation around, but the outlook isn't positive.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: That violent Catastrophe... just slammed into our front line all of a sudden.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: It's very difficult for us to conduct standard operations in these high-density Originium zones, and the exposed Active Originium clusters greatly limit the maneuverability of our high-speed battleships.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: But, the Sarkaz forces don't seem to be affected much. They... don't care at all. Most of them are already Infected.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: The Nachzehrer's troops are also fielding some witchcraft contraptions we've never seen before. The chaotic fissures they spew out are... tricky to deal with. We're still looking for countermeasures.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Hold the line. Have the artillery in the rear lay suppressive fire, and open up a gap to the east.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: It shall be done, milord.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: No mercy for poor Windermere eh, Duke Wellington?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: She just bailed out the fleet we sent to claim our plaything, and you're going to repay the favor by driving the Sarkaz onto her turf?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: I don't remember giving you permission to tap into my communications, Caster.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Stiff as always, aren't you?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I will remind Windermere to take adequate preparations. After all, we are still Victorians.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I know what you're after, old Wellington.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You're getting ahead of yourself.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Next time, I hope you'll find a more appropriate manner of exchanging ideas with me.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Your Grace, you shouldn't continue standing on the deck like this. Though we're a fair distance away from where the Catastrophe struck, the dust can't be good for your health.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: This is my duty, Your Royal Highness Eblana.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You are always worthy of my trust.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Haha... Those two siblings are being extremely cautious.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: This is not the full extent of The Shard's might. They either don't want us to know that they haven't fully mastered the storm's power, or... they're waiting for a better opportunity.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: This storm should've belonged to Victoria alone, but now, we will be first to face it.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I hear the officers murmuring amongst themselves nervously, Your Grace, but you don't seem flustered.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: If anything... you seem to be rather excited?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Indeed, milady. I won't deny it.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: This battlefield commands fear and respect.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: When is the last time I've faced an enemy like this since Gaul's Vieux Vanguard?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: We've long been ready for this. Regardless of whose hands it is in, the storm will only serve to wash away hesitation and weakness from the Tarans, and it shall temper our young troops.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: I can see him... The Nachzehrer King.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Let us drop all pretense and face each other in battle.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: The Tarans will not be stopped here. Our rage is no less than yours.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Your Royal Highness Eblana, I shall secure a future for you and the Taran people.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: My faithful Duke...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Very soon, the final chapter will be written.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Welcome, Lady Ermengarde. With your arrival comes the goodwill of the Liches.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We will never forget. At the moment the Sarkaz needed unity the most, the Liches chose to leave their library and stand at our side.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Hehe. No need to be so formal, Your Highness. I am simply an observer.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But, you still brought us a gift, and the soldiers on the front lines will put it to good use.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: It is but a trifling trick to play with the fissures.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The liches' mastery over dimensional space transcends most people's cognition.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Naturally, unlike your people who've always been in Kazdel, we liches are keen on self-preservation, always looking for a place to hide our phylactery.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But, the Lich's throne has never been removed from the Royal Court's chamber.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: We appreciate Your Highness's thoughtfulness.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I assume you know that Kal'tsit paid me a visit on my way here?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: She tried hard to convince me... not to take your side.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: The young master of the Elegiac Court is fighting alongside them. I've heard the teachers say before that the Banshees' strength is not to be overlooked.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Dame Kal'tsit claimed that the war you and the Regent started will only push these lands into irreversible disorder and strife.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: These things are only temporary. We... have no choice but to endure.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This is the only way the consensus needed for solidarity can be built.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Want to know what the funniest thing is, Your Highness?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Your words sound just like hers.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You both call for unity. You both tell me that this is the only way to avert the impending calamity.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Then, why do the two of you stand in opposition?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Perhaps because... we're both in a hurry.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Rest assured, as a Messenger of the Lich King's Court, I didn't make any promises to Dame Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Just like how I haven't made any promises with you.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: We Liches are never in a hurry to pick a side for ourselves.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: These languishing pains and broken hearts... At long last, they will eventually have a home to return to.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Not much longer now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, will you be able to find that path?

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Damn those officers! They'd rather bring along a tuskbeast than us!

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Who the hell does he think he is? Back in the days, before I got sick, he didn't even dare look me in the eyes!

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Damn it, damn it all! This bloody Oripathy!

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: I'd rather go without those Rhodes Island peoples' inhibitors, and blow up in a cloud of Originium Dust over in Norport!

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: At least, I'd be able to give those freeloading bastards a faceful! They'd get a good taste of what I'm going through too!

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Hah! That Cautus gave me an inhibitor too...

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: These bloody pills aren't gonna save shit!

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: ...I'm done for.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: I can't leave this place.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: My life... isn't worth a damn thing.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: What was the point o' crawling outta Norport? These damn crystals... These damn Originium crystals in my body!

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Run me through, dammit! Run me through already!
The Infected citizen angrily scratches at the Originium crystals on his arm, as if crushing them would make everything go back to normal.

Severe pain rips through him, and the newly-infected person gasps for breath. He is overwhelmed by the pain that had just become familiar to him, and a mixture of tears and sweat rolls down his cheeks.
He lies on his back in a patch of mud. Before his eyes, the sun has risen to its zenith.
Before he closes his eyes, a strand of pink hair suddenly breaks into his vision.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: This is no place to be sunbathing, sir. The mud's going to get in your clothes.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Get away from me. I'm an Infected, and might explode any minute now.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Hah, if I had to guess, I don't think you've had Oripathy for more than a week. Everyone looks just like you the first few days.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Shock and denial, pain and guilt, anger and depression...

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: In the end, they have no choice but to accept that they're a miserable, hapless lot.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: The hell do you know? You're–

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Also an Infected. What's so strange about that?

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: You're also an Infected? But, you look so...

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Wait, I've seen you before...

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Hello, sir. My name is Percival, and I'm the doorman at the Sunset Street Hotel.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: It's a shame, but it seems you don't have much luggage for me to carry.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: No, I meant... in Norport...

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Hmm? Now that is awfully quaint.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: I was with the Mounted Police for quite a few years, Miss Percival. I've been involved in a number of cases, some of which involved the Infected as well.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Hah, I should've thought twice about how I treated 'em back then. Now, I'm one of them.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: I've heard of an organization whose activities have reached even the doors of Londinium.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: If I remember properly, they were called...

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Percival? What are you doing here?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Oh, Red.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I found an Infected on the side of the road. Must've been one of those people thrown here by the Duke of Windermere.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Another one?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Truth be told though, Percival, had you not sent out the news that the separation sequence between Norport and Londinium was underway, the fate of these Infected people might've been even more miserable.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Heh heh, I've always been a sharp one, and quite proud of it!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Thanks to you figuring it out, you even managed to hide our comms as a Londinium public broadcast. You should be glad I have the good habit of tuning into the radio.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: It's not as easy as you make it sound. I had to dismantle the communication station in the hotel before I could finally find a place to pass on the news.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: But, Rhodes Island and that Delphine lady did get the short end of the stick as a result...

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Who exactly are you people...?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Have you ever heard of 'Reunion?'

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Reunion?! Did you just say–

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Woah, the whole gang's here.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Well done, Percival. We've taken in a number of Infected persons along the way, and they're doing much better than we initially expected.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Red was doing most of the hard work. I've pretty much just been slacking off.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: And though I don't want to admit it, Rhodes Island also played a big part.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Rhodes Island... So, they're here too.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: Reunion... I know what you people have done.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: What kind of disaster are you trying to invite upon Victoria this time?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: You have the wrong idea, sir.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: We are the ones who gathered the debris from the ashes of the previous Reunion.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: But, we are no longer what we used to be.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: We will not abandon the name, nor the sins it carries. We must remember our past mistakes, but must also set out once more to prove ourselves to the Infected.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: The new Reunion no longer needs a leader. We've traveled across several countries, fighting side-by-side with the Infected peoples who see themselves as our comrades.

steps.name: Infected Citizen
steps.text: What exactly are you trying to do?

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Medicine and compassion cannot help the Infected in a way that matters, but solidary and strength can.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Sir, the Infected have no country of their own, so the new Reunion shall be where they belong.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Interested in joining us?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Talulah? What are you looking at?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The lingering Catastrophe cloud. The Shard has been activated.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Ugh, there's gonna be a lot more Infected soon.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I also have a message for you, Talulah.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I saw... a Draco who wielded purple flames.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Did you now...?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Percival, I often find myself thinking these days–

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Indeed, there's a certain kind of person that seems naturally born to make waves. They will claim to be their catalysts, leaders, and creators.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: In a sense, they tend to find success... but I would never call them winners.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I refuse to accept... that everything they've made deserves to enter the annals of 'history.'

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I refuse to accept it.
